messages:
alex: Heads-up — ran the nightly matrix for attention kernels across SM80/SM90 + CUDA 12.1/12.3. Seeing a consistent perf regression for our fused-attn kernel on SM90 when sequence >= 1024. Throughput down ~15% and p99 up from ~48ms to ~72ms.
maria: Ugh. Is this the Triton variant or our custom CUDA kernel?
alex: Happens for the Triton fused kernel and our fallback CUDA fused path too. FlashAttention variant (flash_v2) still looks OK. Root cause looks like higher register pressure on SM90 causing fewer warps per SM for long sequences. nvprof traces show more register spills.
sam: Can you paste the micro numbers?
alex: Sure — small paste: 
```
model: gpt-medium
batch: dynamic up to 8
seq: 2048
kernel: fused_attn_triton
SM80 CUDA12.1: tokens/s = 520k, p99 = 48ms
SM90 CUDA12.3: tokens/s = 442k, p99 = 72ms
flash_v2 (triton): SM90 tokens/s = 585k, p99 = 44ms
custom-cuda-fused: SM90 tokens/s = 450k, p99 = 70ms
memory: +0.8GB on SM90 for fused path
```
maria: Interesting that flash_v2 wins on SM90. Maybe our fused implementation uses warp-level reductions that are slower on SM90 due to vectorized loads?
jen: Also check KV cache behavior — did you see more cache writes or re-syncs around long generation? We had a bug that causes extra memcpy on page boundary.
alex: Good call. I instrumented KV writes: for seq>=1024 there are spikes in CPU->GPU copies in the fused path (likely because of our paged-KV eviction checks triggering). Flash avoids that by streaming in tiles.
sam: So two factors: register pressure + extra KV copy path. Which is dominant?
alex: From ablation runs: with KV-copy disabled, fused SM90 improves back ~7% but still behind flash. Disabling some fusion reductions (i.e., fall back to pairwise softmax) removes the remaining gap. So both matter.
maria: What about CUDA versions? Does CUDA12.1 on SM90 behave differently?
alex: I tried SM90 on CUDA12.1 — slightly better than 12.3 for fused (tokens/s ~468k) but still worse than flash. So not purely CUDA runtime.
jen: Can we tweak compiler flags / register allocation? e.g., `-maxrregcount` or split kernels to reduce live registers?
sam: We tried `maxrregcount=64` on custom-cuda-fused — it lowers register pressure but increases instruction count; net throughput was flat. Might need algorithmic split.
alex: Proposed short-term mitigations: 
- Route SM90 long-seq requests to flash_v2 by default (policy tweak).
- Disable the KV eviction check for fused path and rely on periodic background pager for now.
- Add a canary in Dedicated to run fused vs flash and auto-roll back if regression >10%.
maria: Sounds reasonable. Any perf test scripts so others can reproduce?
alex: Yep run this locally: 
```
# reproducible harness
python tools/bench_tokens.py --model gpt-medium --kernel fused_attn_triton --seq 2048 --batch 8 --device sm90
```
perf-bot: nightly-bench reported: eng-runtime/fused-attn-sm90 regression detected (median -14.8%). Ticket #INF-2147 created.
sam: For longer-term: we should build a SM-arch-aware kernel selector. Kernel metadata could include "reg_pressure_estimate" and "kv_copy_friendly" tags. Scheduler picks flash vs fused by estimated seq and hardware.
jen: Also add microbench for paged attention page sizes (32k/64k/128k) — maybe tuning page size eliminates the copy spike.
maria: Action items: alex to open a PR with routing change + disable KV eviction check behind flag; sam to spec kernel metadata and selector; jen to add paged-attn microbench; I'll own the canary rollout policy.
alex: Created draft PR: https://git.redwood/inference/pull/7821 — includes flag `RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KV_EVICT` and routing rule. Running extended smoke now.
maria: Perfect. If perf-bot sees >10% regression in canary, auto-revert. :thumbsup:
alex: FYI I'll also add counters to the runtime trace for "kv_copy_bytes" and "reg_spills" so we can correlate in console.
sam: Let's sync tomorrow with a short demo of the benchmark numbers.
jen: Thanks all — good triage.
alex: Closing the loop once canary completes (ETA ~4h).
